manuscript_theme: How Chinese rap lyrics form recognizable lyrical identities through language, cultural reference, and dictionary-estimated written rhyme
source_policy: Retain only directly relevant sources whose bibliographic metadata and substantive relevance can be verified through an official publisher page and/or publisher-deposited Crossref record.
recommendation: Integrate eight sources as a compact domain strand. Use them to motivate lyrical repertoire and cultural-reference analysis while tightening the boundary against identity, biography, authenticity, and performed-flow claims.

sources.title: Hip-Hopping Across China: Intercultural Formulations of Local Identities
sources.relevance: Interviews, lyric analysis, studio observation, and performance observation show that global hip-hop resources are recruited for locally significant practices in China; this supports a repertoire framing rather than a pure-style vector.
sources.claim_boundary: Does not justify equating a source-credit label with a coherent, stable real-world identity.
sources.suggested_placement: Related Work near the definition of lyrical repertoire.

sources.title: “I am not a qualified dialect rapper”: constructing hip-hop authenticity in China
sources.relevance: The study shows that a local variety, Putonghua, and English acquire meaning through contextualized orders of authenticity, warning against treating automated language proportions as identity or authenticity scores.
sources.claim_boundary: Never infer authenticity from code choice, dialect markers, or embedding similarity alone.
sources.suggested_placement: Related Work on repertoire versus identity and the ethnographic-evidence limitation.

sources.title: Alternative Voice and Local Youth Identity in Chinese Local-Language Rap Music
sources.relevance: Close reading and fieldwork show that regional language, slang, local knowledge, and representations of city or region are substantive resources in Chinese rap, motivating cultural-reference analysis and lexical-semantic fusion.
sources.claim_boundary: A place mention can be a lyrical localization resource but does not establish residence, origin, membership, or affiliation.
sources.suggested_placement: Related Work between language repertoire and cultural-reference extraction; Discussion of label-place edges.

sources.title: Language, identity and unintelligibility: A case study of the rap group Higher Brothers
sources.venue: East Asian Journal of Popular Culture
sources.relevance: The Higher Brothers case separates written language choice from the vocal production and sonic unintelligibility through which local, national, and global identities are negotiated.
sources.claim_boundary: Transcript-only analysis cannot infer performed intelligibility, accent, mumble-rap delivery, or global/local identity.
sources.suggested_placement: Related Work on multilingual repertoire and audio/performance limitations.

sources.title: Constructing ‘corrupted village wives and urban men’ through multilingual performances
sources.relevance: The analysis shows how languages, named places, landmarks, objects, and self-reference jointly localize an ironic rap persona, making it a direct conceptual anchor for evidence-graded cultural-reference edges.
sources.claim_boundary: A statistically supported label-place edge remains a lyric-reference association, not evidence of hometown, residence, cultural membership, friendship, or collaboration.
sources.suggested_placement: Cultural-reference Related Work and the RQ2 Discussion.

sources.title: Rhyming style, persona, and the contested landscape of authentic Chinese hip hop
sources.relevance: Quantitative rhyme description is joined with language use, visuals, themes, performance, and audience reaction to analyze persona, establishing rhyme as one component of a broader semiotic repertoire.
sources.claim_boundary: A 17-class written-ending predictor cannot infer persona or authenticity without the multimodal and interactional evidence used in the source study.
sources.suggested_placement: Rhyme Related Work and Discussion of the negative source-label ablation.

sources.title: Variation is the way to perfection: imperfect rhyming in Chinese hip hop
sources.relevance: The study documents traditional Chinese, rock-rhyme, Southern Mandarin, and Chinese-accented English strategies that can increase perceived rhymability beyond fixed dictionary classes.
sources.claim_boundary: Same-family pinyin endings are not necessarily true performed rhymes, and different-family endings are not necessarily non-rhymes.
sources.suggested_placement: Rhyme Related Work and first paragraph of Rhyme Limitations.

sources.title: Linguistic tone in Chinese rap: an interdisciplinary approach
sources.relevance: An audio-based Tonal Congruence Index over more than 8,000 syllables and 140 Mandarin rap songs, plus rapper interviews, directly demonstrates that tone realization and English use for flow are performance-sensitive phenomena.
sources.claim_boundary: Written pinyin endings cannot measure tonal preservation, cadence, beat alignment, subgenre performance, or flow.
sources.suggested_placement: Final paragraph of Rhyme Related Work and Rhyme Limitations.

bibliographic_year_notes: Cite Liu et al. as 2023 when using the assigned volume 52(4) issue year; the version of record appeared online on 2024-03-29.
Cite Lin and Wang as 2024 for volume 28(2); the version of record appeared online in 2023.
Cite Baioud as 2024 for volume 53(1); the article appeared online in 2023.

Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata dates Wang's Sociolinguistic Studies article to 2013; some secondary bibliographies show 2012, so the final manuscript must use one verified version-of-record year consistently.
integration_plan: Use Barrett, Wang, Liu 2014, and Liu 2021 in one compact paragraph establishing localized, mixed, and performed repertoire.
Use Baioud to motivate the cultural meaning and strict interpretation boundary of place/reference edges.
Use Lin and Wang, Wang and Lin, and Liu et al. as the three-source chain for rhyme-plus-persona, imperfect/performed rhyme, and tone/audio boundaries.
Do not add scene-level claims about censorship, gender, race, or audience reception unless the manuscript introduces evidence for those questions.
